addiction.abstain_intro_p1: No weekly milestone, no dose to respect. Just one thing: hold on.
addiction.abstain_intro_p2: Every day, you mark “day held” or “I consumed”. The counter goes up. In case of relapse, it resets to zero — but your previous record stays visible. The work you’ve done does not disappear.
addiction.abstain_intro_p3: Symbolic milestones are reached automatically: 24h, 72h, 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, 6 months, 1 year…

addiction.timer_message: Set it down for 10 minutes — the emergency almost always passes.
addiction.timer_done_message: It passed. You held on. — Well done.
timer_messages: Breathe. The feeling is real, but it passes.
Withdrawal is physical. Observing it is enough.
You don’t have to do anything — just wait.
One more minute. That’s all we ask.
addiction.urge_subtitle: Surf the urge instead of fighting it — a short guided session.
addiction.urge_modal_subtitle: Observe the urge without acting. It rises, it crests, it falls back down.
addiction.urge_step1_text:
Stop what you’re doing.
Sit comfortably, close your eyes if you want.

Take three slow deep breaths.
addiction.urge_step2_text:
Where do you feel the urge in your body?
Throat, chest, belly, hands?

Don’t judge. Just observe where it’s happening.
addiction.urge_step3_text:
Is it warm? Cold? Tight? Pulsing?
Does it move or is it fixed?

Put words to the sensation — like a curious observer.
addiction.urge_step4_text:
Imagine sending your breath directly toward that area.
Inhale… exhale… slowly.

You’re not trying to make it go away. You’re letting it be there.
addiction.urge_step5_text:
The urge is a wave: it rises, reaches a peak, then falls back down.
You don’t need to act. Just surf.

Stay here a little longer. You already held on — that’s the victory.

linear.name: Linear
linear.tagline: Steady reduction, same amount each week.
linear.hint: Predictable, balanced. A good default option.

soft.name: Gentle
soft.tagline: A little at the beginning, more at the end.
soft.hint: Gives you time to adapt — useful if getting started feels scary.

standard.name: Standard
standard.tagline: Gentle at the beginning, strong in the middle, gentle at the end.
standard.hint: The balance of the original plan. Breaks inertia without making the end too harsh.

aggressive.name: Aggressive
aggressive.tagline: A lot at the beginning, little at the end.
aggressive.hint: Rip the band-aid off. The initial slope is hard, but the end is very reachable.

abstain_milestones.label: 24 hours
abstain_milestones.note: The first day. Often the hardest.

abstain_milestones.label: 72 hours
abstain_milestones.note: Peak physical withdrawal for many addictions. It eases after that.

abstain_milestones.label: 7 days
abstain_milestones.note: First week. The body starts to regulate itself.

abstain_milestones.label: 14 days
abstain_milestones.note: Two weeks. Sleep often starts coming back at this stage.

abstain_milestones.label: 30 days
abstain_milestones.note: First month. A clear threshold — the urge recedes, breathing room comes back.

abstain_milestones.label: 60 days
abstain_milestones.note: Second month. New automatic habits start settling in.

abstain_milestones.label: 90 days
abstain_milestones.note: Three months. A lot of literature talks about neurological stabilization around this threshold.

abstain_milestones.label: 6 months
abstain_milestones.note: Six months. The brain has had time to reorganize itself more durably.

abstain_milestones.label: 1 year
abstain_milestones.note: One year. This is new territory.
